headlines.article_text: Boeing-Lockheed rocket fails mid-flight, destroying Amazon satellites Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu In this article AMZN Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT A United Launch Alliance (ULA) Vulcan VC6L rocket lifts off from Space Launch Complex-41 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida on Nov. 15, 2026, carrying 40 Amazon Leo broadband satellites on the Leo Vulcan 1 (LV-01) mission. The mission and all 40 satellites were lost after the rocket suffered an anomaly about 10 minutes into flight, according to ULA. It was Vulcan's first flight in nine months, following a solid rocket booster anomaly in February 2026, and the first of 38 Vulcan launches contracted by Amazon. It was also the first Vulcan to fly with six solid rocket boosters. Nurphoto | Nurphoto | Getty Images A Vulcan rocket owned by United Launch Alliance, the ⁠joint venture of Boeing and Lockheed Martin , failed on Sunday shortly after liftoff from Florida, destroying its payload of 40 satellites from Amazon's Leo internet network in the launch company's first mission failure. The rocket ​failed roughly 10 minutes after liftoff from the Cape ​Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida, and ​the cause was not immediately clear. It represented a major setback for the two-decade-old company's new flagship rocket as ULA sought to begin a regular launch cadence for Amazon's burgeoning satellite internet constellation. "Based on data received by our Launch Director, we confirm that the Vulcan vehicle launched from Space Launch Complex 41 suffered an anomaly 10 minutes ⁠into the ‌flight and failed to deliver the Amazon mission to orbit," ULA said in a ⁠statement. "Every flight generates data, and every flight teaches us something. Since the anomaly just occurred, we don't have any specific data yet to understand what occurred today," ULA said. The failure is expected to lead to a lengthy technical investigation that would keep the rocket off the market for months. This could deepen a US launch bottleneck brought on by other rocket mishaps and challenges across ‌the industry as well as the looming retirement of SpaceX's Falcon 9, the world's most active rocket. SpaceX is no longer accepting bookings for the Falcon 9. "There is risk with any launch, and that's especially true for inaugural missions like LV-01," Amazon said in a statement, referring to ​Sunday's mission. "ULA has been a trusted partner for Amazon, and we believe they'll learn from this mission and deliver on their long-term plans for Vulcan." The Sunday flight was Vulcan's fifth since its 2024 debut and first in nine months, following a launch hiatus drawn out by separate technical investigations into its solid rocket side boosters and its core BE-4 engines, which are supplied by Amazon founder Jeff Bezos' Blue ⁠Origin space company. Blue Origin is working with ULA in the investigation into Sunday's failure, according to a person familiar with the matter who spoke on condition of anonymity. The boosters were being ‌scrutinized for issues encountered on Vulcan's last two flights, including a mission in February for the U.S. Space ‌Force. Both missions successfully delivered their payloads to orbit, but the Pentagon had not yet approved the rocket to resume flying national security payloads, pending its performance on Sunday's Amazon mission. Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket with the BE-4 engine had a launchpad explosion in May, and its investigation determined the engine was the cause. That led the company to modify the engines delivered to ULA for Vulcan, ULA spokesperson Jessica Rye told Reuters in August. It was unclear if the BE-4 engines played a role ⁠in Sunday's mission failure. It appeared to occur after the separation of Vulcan's second stage, the portion carrying the Amazon satellites, from the ⁠first-stage booster powered by the BE-4 engines. ULA was formed in 2006 in a merger of Boeing's Delta rocket program and Lockheed Martin's Atlas rocket program. The company has maintained a 100% mission success record ever since. Its Delta and Atlas rockets ​had only suffered a handful of failures in the decades before the merger. Amazon's elusive access to space The failure is another setback for Amazon as it races to deploy satellites using third-party launch providers, many of which have had groundings and failures. The New Glenn explosion in May happened days before it was due to launch Amazon Leo satellites. The rocket failures have repeatedly delayed Amazon's bid to rival SpaceX's vast Starlink internet network, which has more than 11,000 satellites and millions of customers worldwide. SpaceX's wide lead over its satellite rivals is due in part to the advantage of having its own rocket to launch its satellites, ​while other companies spend billions of dollars on external launches. Since ‌2025, 398 Leo satellites have been deployed across 14 launches, about 12% of the 3,236 satellites Amazon needs for global service coverage. headlines.title: Stocks making the biggest moves Monday: L3Harris, Nvidia, Take-Two Interactive, Yeti, American Airlines & more
headlines.summary: Follow along as CNBC highlights the biggest stock market moves of the day.
headlines.article_text: Stocks moving the most today: Live updates Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Visual China Group | Getty Images Nvidia shares were under pressure once again on Monday, with traders bracing for the company's quarterly report due postmarket Tuesday. Other stocks making moves include Take-Two Interactive, as gamers await the release of "Grand Theft Auto VI", and Yeti Holdings, which pulled back following an analyst downgrade. Follow along as CNBC highlights the biggest stock market moves of the day. 1 Hour Ago Tyson Foods rallies on earnings beat Shares of Tyson Foods advanced more than 9% on better-than-expected quarterly results. The company delivered earnings per share of 61 cents on revenue of $14.59 billion. Analysts polled by FactSet expected a profit of 53 cents per share on revenue of $14.1 billion. Tyson is known for its portfolio of food products which include beef, pork, chicken, and prepared foods. To be sure, the company's guidance for fiscal 2027 was cause for some pause. Management expects operating income of $1.7 billion to $2.15 billion, which is in line with FactSet's $2.13 billion estimate. The company also expects beef production to decrease by about 2% next year and anticipates an operating income loss in the segment. — Paulina Likos 3 Hours Ago L3Harris drops 4% after U.S. blames contractor for Friday's nationwide groundstop The New York Stock Exchange welcomes L3Harris Technologies on April 23rd, 2026. NYSE L3Harris , a defense electronics contractor, fell 4% after the Trump administration blamed it for Friday's nearly five-hour nationwide groundstop of all airline traffic. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy on Saturday said the ground stop occurred while L3Harris was performing routine maintenance. "This was an FAA system that didn't meet the moment," Duffy said at a press conference. Cancelation rates for the top six U.S. airlines reached 32% Friday and 30% on Saturday, according to FlightAware data analyzed by UBS. L3Harris shares over the past five days — Ananya Chetia 3 Hours Ago Johnson & Johnson edges higher after acquiring Ollin Biosciences Shares for Johnson & Johnson gained 1.4% after the company announced it will acquire clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company Ollin Biosciences for $2.2 billion. Johnson & Johnson also announced it will receive $750 million from Blackstone Life Sciences to fully cover the Phase 3 development of OLN324, an "investigational, next-generation bispecific antibody." — Ananya Chetia 3 Hours Ago Shares for Aramark tumble over 5% following earnings Shares for Aramark fell more than 5% after the company posted fiscal fourth-quarter results that missed the expectations. The operator of cafeterias, hospital kitchens and sports stadium food stands reported adjusted earnings per share of 71 cents on revenue of $5.29 billion. Analysts polled by FactSet expected a profit of 75 cents per share on revenue of $5.03 billion. The company also expects adjusted earnings per share to increase between 20% and 25% and revenue to grow between 9% and 10% for the full year. — Ananya Chetia 4 Hours Ago Top airline shares down after Friday's nationwide ground stop of flights Passengers queue at the Southwest Airlines desk to speak with a representative at Eppley Airfield in Omaha, Neb., on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026. Nikos Frazier | Omaha World-Herald | Lee Newspapers | Getty Images Shares related to airlines, including American Airlines , Delta and United Airlines were down over 1% after the Federal Aviation Administration briefly issued a nationwide ground stop on all flights on Friday, causing flight delays and travel disruptions. On Sunday, President Donald Trump blamed the Biden administration for the FAA stop. "The Biden Administration was an FAA disaster. Everything they touched turned bad," he wrote on social media. — Ananya Chetia 4 Hours Ago StoneX upgrades Stagwell to buy from hold Shares of Stagwell popped over 1% after StoneX upgraded the digital-first marketing company to buy from hold. "Our Boston-hosted NDR last wk with CEO Mark Penn left us more optimistic on Enterprise tech solutions top line and incremental margin prospects," wrote analyst Alex Lavigne. Lavigne added while its concerned Stagwell is losing small and midsize business customers, he has a positive outlook that its growing technology and other higher-margin businesses will be profitable and make up for those losses. Lavigne set Stagwell's price target to $15, implying a 33% upside from Friday's close. — Ananya Chetia 4 Hours Ago SpaceX gains slightly after successfully catching upper stage of Starship SpaceX Starship 42 returns from orbit to the launch pad on the 15th test flight from the SpaceX launch complex in Starbase, Texas, US, November 14, 2026. Joe Skipper | Reuters SpaceX gained slightly after its spacecraft was able to catch the upper stage portion of its Starship rocket from orbit . This comes after the first phase of the flight on Friday was unsuccessful, with SpaceX unable to catch and recover the rocket's booster and exploding before it fell into the Gulf of Mexico. spcx — Ananya Chetia 5 Hours Ago Yeti falls after Goldman Sachs downgrade Yeti dropped 1.3% after Goldman Sachs downgraded the beverage container manufacturer to neutral from buy. "While our checks ahead of the print pointed to a more measured backdrop, YETI's 3Q update revealed a more meaningful softening in US DTC growth momentum. In combination with our forecast for US wholesale to slow following wholesale replenishment, we now see a tougher sales backdrop ahead for the US business which we believe will limit multiple expansion for the stock," wrote analyst Brooke Roach. — Fred Imbert 5 Hours Ago Take-Two Interactive rises ahead of 'Grand Theft Auto VI' release Commuters walk past advertising billboards for the game "Grand Theft Auto VI" in a hallway at Kings Cross underground station, in central London on November 11, 2026. Henry Nicholls | Afp | Getty Images Take-Two Interactive shares were up more than 3% ahead of Thursday's release of the much-anticipated "Grand Theft Auto VI" video game. Jefferies over the weekend also reiterated its buy rating and $300 price target on Take-Two, saying "GTA VI is just the beginning." "While the launch itself is well understood, we believe the bigger opportunity is the duration of the GTA VI monetization cycle. GTA Online and an eventual PC release could provide meaningful incremental bookings into FY28, neither of which we believe is embedded in FY27 guidance. We continue to model FY27 bookings above the high end of guidance and see upside to our $10 FY28 EPS estimate as the GTA VI ecosystem scales," wrote analyst James Heaney. TTWO YTD — Fred Imbert 5 Hours Ago Nvidia falls again to start the week Nvidia shares were down 2.2%, adding to their steep losses from last week, as traders brace for the company's fiscal third-quarter results due Tuesday.
